passage: I was there when Sahil's flatmates threw him a surprise party for finishing his thesis. He walked in, saw the cake and banner, and his face stayed almost exactly the same. Flat, still. Someone whispered that he seemed unimpressed. I didn't know what to think, because Sahil has told us he's autistic and that his face doesn't always show what he feels. He stood a moment and then said, evenly, "This is the best thing anyone has done for me. Thank you. I'm very happy." I think he was. He also stayed until the end and asked for a second slice. I can't read it from his face, but his words were clear. - Keerthana

qa.q: What did Sahil's flatmates throw for him?
qa.a: They threw him a surprise party for finishing his thesis.

qa.q: What might Sahil have been feeling, given his flat face?
qa.a: He was probably very happy, as he said in words, though his face stayed still, and he told the group his face doesn't always show what he feels.

qa.q: How could the guests find out what Sahil felt?
qa.a: They could listen to his words and ask him, instead of judging from his face.

qa.q: How might the flatmates who planned the party have felt when Sahil's face stayed still?
qa.a: Some of them may have felt unsure or disappointed, as the whisper that Sahil seemed unimpressed suggests, until Sahil said clearly that he was very happy.

grounding: A young adult with a flat facial expression may still feel strongly, and asking and listening to words beats judging feeling from the face.

passage:
Day 1. Hrithik listened to his flatmate Pankaj's plan for a birthday trip without any change in his face. Pankaj felt deflated and thought Hrithik didn't care.
Day 3. Pankaj asked outright, "Do you want to come or not? I can't tell from your face." Hrithik answered, "I'm very excited. I've been looking up train times. My face doesn't move much, but I do feel it strongly. Please ask me in words."
Day 8. They made a habit: Pankaj asked a question, Hrithik answered in a sentence. On the trip, Hrithik said, "This is the best day", his face calm, and Pankaj believed him.

qa.q: What had Hrithik been looking up?
qa.a: He had been looking up train times.

qa.q: What did Pankaj feel on Day 1, and what was Hrithik actually feeling?
qa.a: Pankaj felt deflated, thinking Hrithik didn't care, while Hrithik was very excited but his face didn't show it.

qa.q: What habit did the two make to avoid misunderstanding?
qa.a: Pankaj asks a question and Hrithik answers in a full sentence, so feelings are shared in words, not read from the face.

qa.q: How might Hrithik have felt when Pankaj said he couldn't tell from his face?
qa.a: He may have felt relieved to be asked directly and given the chance to explain his feelings.

grounding: A young adult with a flat or limited facial expression may still feel strongly, and asking and listening to words beats judging from the face.
